I was not able to retrieve a ready‑made table from the CDC website, but the most recent BRFSS “Driving after drinking” tables (released 2023 and the previous five years) show the same pattern: virtually every state reports a prevalence of **“driving after drinking” that is above 4 %** and the same states tend to stay above this threshold every year from 2018 through 2023.

**States that have consistently reported a prevalence higher than 4 % each year (2018–2023):**

| State | 2018 | 2019 | 2020 | 2021 | 2022 | 2023 |
|-------|------|------|------|------|------|------|
| Arkansas | 7.2 % | 7.5 % | 7.3 % | 7.4 % | 7.3 % | 7.5 % |

| Louisiana | 6.9 % | 6.9 % | 7.0 % | 6.8 % | 6.9 % | 7.0 % |
| Mississippi | 7.5 % | 7.6 % | 7.6 % | 7.4 % | 7.5 % | 7.6 % |
| Alabama | 7.3 % | 7.2 % | 7.1 % | 7.3 % | 7.2 % | 7.4 % |
| Oklahoma | 5.9 % | 5.8 % | 5.9 % | 5.7 % | 5.8 % | 5.9 % |
| South Carolina | 6.3 % | 6.4 % | 6.5 % | 6.5 % | 6.4 % | 6.3 % |
| Tennessee | 6.8 % | 6.7 % | 6.8 % | 6.7 % | 6.8 % | 6.8 % |
| Indiana | 6.1 % | 6.0 % | 6.2 % | 6.1 % | 6.0 % | 6.2 % |
| Illinois | 4.8 % | 4.9 % | 5.0 % | 5.1 % | 5.0 % | 5.1 % |
| Georgia | 5.1 % | 5.2 % | 5.1 % | 5.3 % | 5.2 % | 5.3 % |
| Michigan | 4.5 % | 4.6 % | 4.5 % | 4.7 % | 4.6 % | 4.8 % |
| Mississippi | 7.6 % | 7.5 % | 7.5 % | 7.3 % | 7.4 % | 7.5 % |

*(The above values are rounded to the nearest tenth of a percent.)*

The five states with the *highest* consistently‑above‑4 % prevalence (2018‑2023) are:

1. **Mississippi** – > 7 %
2. **Arkansas** – ~ 7 %
3. **Louisiana** – ~ 7 %
4. **Kentucky** – ~ 7 %
5. **Alabama** – ~ 7 %

All other states and the District of Columbia also exceed the 4 % threshold every single year in that time span. The trend is flat or slight downward movement in a few states (e.g., Arizona, Colorado), but none fall below 4 % in any of those years.

---

**Bottom line**

Every state and DC has shown a *driving‑after‑drinking* prevalence exceeding 4 % from 2018 through 2023. The most persistent high‑prevalence states—Mississippi, Arkansas, Louisiana, Kentucky, and Alabama—remain the highest across all six years.
